title: "And make a beacon": UAP experts attempt to summon orbs in UFO hotspot related to infamous Bass Strait disappearance
excerpt: In the latest episode of Reality Check with Ross Coulthart on NewsNation, UAP experts have attempted to summon orbs in a UFO hotspot.
content:
In the latest episode of Reality Check with Ross Coulthart on NewsNation, UAP experts have attempted to summon orbs in a UFO hotspot. They chose a location linked to the infamous Bass Strait Disappearance. Coulthart visited the UAP hotspot to investigate the controversial practice of CE5 (Close Encounters of the Fifth Kind), also called neuromeditative signalling. Coulthart joined the team from Whitehawk Psionics, who believe that they can use meditation and intention to invite anomalous golden orbs.

During the second contact attempt, Troy Gavin explains the process begins with a clearing by visualizing a shield to avoid negative distractions, followed by the invitation where the participants are required to shoot a column of light from their heart or chest. He describes this step as:

"And make a beacon. That can go out into the solar system, into the atmosphere, however far you want."

He further explains:

"That sends out a signal and then we do that in reverse...whereas we'll look back similar to looking back on a Google Earth. Imagine you're the satellite looking at the planet and you're looking down from a Google Earth perspective. So we do that, send out the signal and look back at the location where we are somewhere in the middle is where we find some of this NHI might be able to tap in or communicate."

Throughout the video, the team explains their process, which includes achieving heart coherence through meditation, setting a protective intention, and projecting a mental signal to the universe to invite contact. The team uses tools like LeoLabs satellite tracking, Stellarium, and FlightRadar to rule out prosaic objects like drones, satellites, planets, and planes.

UAP experts attempt CE5 experiment at Bass Strait UFO hotspot for Ross Coulthart's UFO files investigation

After the CE5 experiment, the participants explained their individual feelings. Some noted that the experience could get quite intense, as it could bring significant changes to one's feelings and body. One of them noted:

"It just made me feel like there was a presence looking at me and then I was looking back at it."

He claimed it was like a high, energetic feeling. The team, however, did not capture the 'golden orbs' during filming this segment. They emphasized that the CE5 experiment is not summoning the UFO or UAP activity on command but fostering a state of openness for potential interaction. This experiment highlights the challenges of gathering data on such UAP phenomena.

Why did Whitehawk Psionics choose Bass Strait to conduct the CE5 experiment?

According to Monument Australia, on the evening of October 21, 1978, a young Australian pilot, Frederick Valentich, disappeared over Bass Strait while flying from Melbourne's Moorabbin Airport to King Island. According to reports, the pilot spotted a UFO following him. He contacted the Melbourne Flight Service Unit to report the incident. Despite an extensive search, neither Valentich nor any wreckage was ever found.

When Coulthart asked why the team chose the Bass Strait UFO hotspot as the site for the experiment, Troy Gavin explained that the team has seen or received reports of anomalous UAP activity in that location. He added that there is talk about USOs and that the US Navy has been reporting stuff around the coast of California. He questioned whether there might be an ongoing unexplained presence in the waters of Bass Strait.
